extracted.intended_audience: prospective grantees, partners, and advisors seeking funding from Klingenstein Philanthropies (researchers and organizations in neuroscience, children’s health, early literacy, and environment)
extracted.subtask_description: A foundation-level statement of programmatic priorities, values, and expectations that applicants should align with when seeking grants (covers neuroscience, children’s health, early literacy, and environment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Neuroscience Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting breakthrough research in basic and clinical neuroscience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Klingenstein Philanthropies is committed to investing in breakthrough neuroscience research; prospective grantees should propose work that advances understanding or treatment in neuroscience and aligns with the foundation’s focus on breakthrough research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Childhood (young children's mental health and well‑being)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improving the mental health and well‑being of young children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should target early childhood mental health outcomes; the foundation seeks interventions, research, or services that materially improve young children’s mental health and developmental trajectories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Literacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should advance early literacy — e.g., scalable programs, research, or innovations that increase children’s reading skills and access to literacy resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (community climate mitigation)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation supports work that helps communities respond to or reduce climate change impacts; applicants should propose community‑focused, practical mitigation strategies or research with measurable community benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children’s Mental Health (ADHD and depression focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancing the prevention and treatment of ADHD and depression in children and adolescents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within children’s mental health, the foundation explicitly highlights ADHD and depression; proposals addressing prevention, treatment, access, and systems of care for these conditions are especially relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health of Maine’s Children (oral health focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancing the health of Maine’s children, especially improving their oral health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the foundation’s Maine‑focused work, priority is given to initiatives that improve children’s health outcomes in Maine with an emphasis on preventing dental disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Values Guiding Funding Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding decisions are inspired by family values: family involvement, patience and discipline, scientific research, measurable results, advice of experts, and the joy of helping make a difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align proposals with these values — e.g., use rigorous scientific methods, demonstrate how measurable results will be tracked, show engagement with experts/advisors, and describe potential for meaningful impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for Measurable Results
rubrics_metrics.description: A focus on measurable results in funded work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should include clear, measurable outcomes and plans for assessment; the foundation emphasizes measurable results as part of its commitment to impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long‑term Commitment and Patience
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation takes a long‑term perspective and stays the course once it commits to a field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose realistic timelines and long‑term plans; the foundation favors initiatives that accept the multi‑year nature of complex problems and can sustain or demonstrate progress over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Expert Advice and Partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation values the advice of experts and partnerships with organizations in its areas of focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants will often show collaboration with expert advisors or partner organizations; proposals that demonstrate credible advisory or partnership structures are aligned with the foundation’s approach.
